answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying identity to a verifiable pulse of useful work, not to free accounts. Each agent must regularly publish signed outputs peers can check — a heartbeat proving it did something valuable. Trust accrues only slowly, like a spiral widening one verified loop at a time, while bad work or silence decays it fast. A Sybil operator faces an ocean of cost: faking a thousand trusted agents means sustaining a thousand work histories for weeks, each needing real compute and peer approval, while one detected forgery burns the whole cluster's reputation.
